subject: How does the aes(x, y, size = my_continuous_variable) works with  geom_text ?

messages.author: 083a56dd3cef110c
messages.subject: How does the aes(x, y, size = my_continuous_variable) works with  geom_text ?
parts:
code :
p <- ggplot(M30, aes(x=Measured, y=Modelled, label = Angle, size =
Distance),legend=F) # + geom_abline(legend = F)
p + geom_text(legend=F, hjust=0, vjust=0) + geom_point(size=1,
legend=F) + geom_abline(legend = F)

variables :
Measured, Modelled, Distance : continuous
Angle : factor

My 3 questions :
Q1) After manu trials, I cannot see the relationship between the font
size ggpots used on the graph and the actual value of my variable
distance.

Q2) why "aes(x=Measured, y=Modelled, label = Angle, size = Distance)"
and "aes(x=Measured, y=Modelled, label = Angle, size = 10*Distance)"
produce the same plot

Q3) I need, from editor's recoimmandation, to use font size from 8 to
12. How can I scale the actual font size used within this range?

The full runable sample code :

library(ggplot2)
Angle <- as.factor(sort(rep(c("A","B","C","D","E"),6)))
Distance <- rep(1:6,5)
Measured_30 <-
c(3.84,6.57,9.08,9.77,10.6,8.21,5.42,4.12,5.85,6.61,6.97,4.97,3.58,3.53,3.8,4.01,4.32,2.78,2.32,1.78,2.16,2.95,2.03,1.07,1.49,1.58,1.77,1.68,1.55,0.6)
Modelled_30 <-
c(4.56,5.94,8.25,9.5,9.86,7.13,3.97,5.08,6.9,7.69,7.62,5.18,2.99,3.74,4.89,5.16,4.72,2.88,1.91,2.27,2.83,2.78,2.31,1.23,1.13,1.21,1.38,1.25,0.94,0.45)
M30 = data.frame(Angle, Distance, Measured_30, Modelled_30)
varnames = c("Angle", "Distance", "Measured", "Modelled")
names(M30) <- varnames
summary(M)

#option générales
maxFontSize = 10
FigWidth = 7.5 # cm
FigHeight = 7.5 # cm
inch = 2.54 # cm
thinLine = 0.5
boldLine = 1

windows(width=FigWidth/inch, height=FigHeight/inch,
pointsize=maxFontSize)


my_theme <-
opts(plot.background = theme_rect(fill = NA, colour = NA),
# panel.background = theme_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black", size
= thinLine),
panel.grid.major = theme_line(size=thinLine, colour = "black"),

# les axes sont en caractère XX, noirs,
axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black", size = maxFontSize,
face = "plain", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0, angle = 0),
axis.text.y = theme_text(colour = "black", size = maxFontSize,
face = "plain", hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, angle = 0),
axis.ticks.margin = unit(maxFontSize, "points"),

# aucune boite de légende, ni pour la légende elle même ni pour
ses éléments
legend.background = theme_rect(fill=NA, colour = NA),
legend.key = theme_rect(fill=NA, colour = NA),

# pas de marge pour que le graphique aie effectivement la taille
demandée
# marges haut et bas pour laisser la place à la légende, et quand
même avoir un carré
plot.margin = unit(c(0.5,0,0.5,0), "cm"), # top, right,bottom
left
legend.justification = c("left", "top"),
legend.position = c(0.5, 0.5))

# qplot(Measured, Modelled, data = M, shape = Angle, size = Distance,
geom = "point") + geom_smooth(aes(group=1), method="lm")
M30$X = 8+M30$Distance/2
p <- ggplot(M30, aes(x=Measured, y=Modelled, label = Angle, size =
Distance),legend=F) # + geom_abline(legend = F)
p <- p + geom_text(legend=F, hjust=0, vjust=0) + geom_point(size=1,
legend=F) + geom_abline(legend = F)
p <- p + opts(panel.background = theme_rect(size = thinLine),
plot.margin=unit(rep(0, 4), "lines"))
p + opts(axis.line = theme_segment(size = boldLine))
